\chapter{Tuviera --- the Hard Stems, Collected Free}
\label{ch:tuviera}
\hlchaptermodality{207}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can build the supposing form of the strong verbs without learning a new stem.}

I can build the supposing form of the strong verbs without learning a new stem.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[tuviera]{tuviera}

\label{lesson:ES-C56-tuviera}



\begin{quote}
The rule, again. (Take the \emph{they} past, swap \emph{-ron} for \emph{-ra}.)

Now try it on the verbs that gave you the most trouble.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the hard ones cost nothing}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{they past} & \textbf{supposing} \\
\midrule
tuvieron & \textbf{tuviera} \\
hicieron & \textbf{hiciera} \\
estuvieron & \textbf{estuviera} \\
fueron & \textbf{fuera} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Nothing new was learned here.} The same swap, applied to stems you already had. The four words you memorised for the preterite have now paid for themselves twice.

And \emph{fuera} keeps the double duty \emph{fui} and \emph{fueron} had: it is the supposing form of \emph{\textbf{ser}} \textbf{and} of \emph{\textbf{ir}}. \emph{Si fuera} can begin \emph{if I were} or \emph{if I went}, and only the rest of the sentence decides.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
\textbf{This is what a well-shaped irregularity looks like.}

Spanish could have given the supposing form its own set of broken verbs. Instead it built the form out of one that was already broken, so the damage is paid for once and reused. Learn \emph{tuvieron} and you have \emph{tuviera} for nothing.

Which is why the plural had to come first. It was never only about saying \emph{they had}.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{tuvieron $\to$ tuviera}, \emph{fueron $\to$ fuera}
  \item \emph{hicieron $\to$ hiciera}, \emph{estuvieron $\to$ estuviera}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many new stems? (\textbf{None}.) Which form serves two verbs? (\emph{\textbf{Fuera}}.)

And why did the preterite plural have to come first? (Because \textbf{this form is cut out of it}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
